reason: The scheduling measurement itself was internally byte-identical, but the experiment imported the obsolete attempt-1 CMPNX9 Mosaic portfolio instead of the accepted attempt-5 Residual Program Packing portfolio. Its 47,197,165-byte result selected the exact v0.28 fallback, while accepted attempt #5 produces a smaller 47,147,764-byte hostile aggregate. This record therefore cannot support a v0.29 release-speed claim.

supersession.status: A corrected ABBA scheduler experiment is the only admissible successor.

invalidated_evidence.interpretation: Process-level overlap cleared the preregistered speed hurdle with zero archive-byte change. This remains useful evidence about scheduling potential for the obsolete attempt-1 portfolio, but it is not evidence about the accepted attempt-5 release candidate.

footnote: History is preserved rather than deleted so future audits can see both why the original run looked valid and why engine identity is now a first-class release invariant.
